Klasse Stateful<A,S>

java.lang.Object
org.quurz.foomp.base.util.Stateful<A,S>
Typparameter:
A - the produced value type
S - the state type
Alle implementierten Schnittstellen:
H2Appliable<Stateful.µ, A, S>, H2Bindable<Stateful.µ, A, S>, H2Mappable<Stateful.µ, A, S>, H2Monadic<Stateful.µ, A, S>, org.quurz.foomp.higher.Higher2<Stateful.µ, A, S>, org.quurz.foomp.higher.Hkt<Stateful.µ>
public class Stateful<A,S> extends Object implements H2Monadic<Stateful.µ, A, S>, org.quurz.foomp.higher.Higher2<Stateful.µ, A, S>

Models a classic State monad carrying a state S and producing a value A. Internally this is a function of shape S -> (A, S).

Semantics:

  • map: transforms the produced value, threading the state through unchanged.
  • applyTo (applicative): threads state from the function value to this value: s0 -> (f, s1) <- tf(s0); (a, s2) <- this(s1); result = (f(a), s2).
  • flatMap (flatMap): sequences computations, passing the new state to the next step: s0 -> (a, s1) <- this(s0); next = f(a); result <- next(s1).

Contract: unless stated otherwise, inputs must not be null and results must not be null. Null‑checks are enforced to keep usage safe and predictable.

Examples: 

  // A simple state: an Integer "tick" that increments on each step
  Function<Integer, Tuple2<Boolean, Integer>> run = s -> tuple2((s % 2) == 0, s + 1);
  Stateful<Boolean, Integer> st = Stateful.stateful(run);

  // map: transform the value; state is preserved
  var mapped = st.map(Object::toString);
  mapped.runState(1);   // -> ("false", 2)

  // applyTo: function-in-stateful applied to current value, threading state correctly
  var tf = Stateful.stateful((Integer s) -> tuple2((Function<Boolean, String>) Object::toString, s));
  var lifted = st.applyTo(tf);
  lifted.runState(1);   // -> ("false", 2)

  // flatMap: sequence and pass along the new state
  var bound = st.flatMap(b -> Stateful.stateOf(b ? "even" : "odd"));
  bound.runState(1);    // -> ("odd", 2)

  // Utilities:
  Stateful.putState(42).execState(0); // -> 42
  Stateful.getState().execValue(5);   // -> 5

1.0.0
